subtopics.title: Convert First — the Step That Decides the Mark

questions.question: One square metre is equal to:
A cubic metre of water is:
2 400 mm expressed in metres is:
Which pair of habits does the lesson name as protecting measurement marks?
options: Write the unit on every line, and round only once at the end
Estimate first, then check with a calculator
Round each step to two decimals as you go

subtopics.title: Fencing the Garden — Perimeter as a Shopping List

questions.question: The perimeter of a garden 12 m by 8 m is:
38 m of mesh is needed and rolls hold 30 m. How many rolls must be bought, and why?
options: 2 rolls, because materials must always be rounded up to cover the job
1,27 rolls, because that is the exact answer

questions.question: Poles stand every 2 m around the closed 40 m boundary. The number of poles is:
options: 20, because a closed boundary needs as many poles as gaps
21, because you always add one pole
19, because the gate replaces a pole

questions.question: The total cost of 2 rolls at R899,00 and 20 poles at R65,00 is:

subtopics.title: Tiles and Paint — Area, Coverage and Waste

questions.question: The floor of a room 4,2 m by 3,5 m has an area of:
With a 10% waste allowance added, 14,7 m² of floor needs how many 1,5 m² boxes of tiles?
The wall area of the room is found by:
options: Length × breadth, the same as the floor
Perimeter of the room × wall height

questions.question: After subtracting the door (1,89 m²) and window (1,8 m²) from 41,58 m², two coats at 8 m² per litre require:

subtopics.title: The Water Tank — Volume, Litres and How Long It Lasts

questions.question: A cylindrical tank is 1,4 m across. The radius used in the formula is:
Using π = 3,142, the volume of the tank (radius 0,7 m, height 1,6 m) is about:
A household of five using 450 ℓ a day empties the 2 463 ℓ tank in:
options: 5 complete days, because the sixth day runs dry

questions.question: A 60 m² roof catching 12 mm of rain collects:

subtopics.title: Walking Around It, Covering It, Filling It

questions.question: "How far around?" is a question about:
Answering 20 m for the perimeter of the 12 m by 8 m garden means the learner:
options: Added the two sides but forgot to double, buying half the fence needed

questions.question: The little raised 3 on a volume answer tells you that:
options: You are counting cubes, because three dimensions were multiplied
The answer must be divided by three

subtopics.title: Buying Enough Paint Without Buying Too Much

questions.question: Buying 2 rolls of 30 m mesh for a 38 m job leaves:
options: 22 m unused, which a good answer mentions as waste

questions.question: Which measurement must NOT be used to work out how much paint the walls need?
The rule stated for buying materials is:
options: Round to the nearest whole number
Round down and buy more later if needed

questions.question: Why is 10% added to the floor area before dividing by the box coverage?
options: Because tiles are cut at the edges and some break
Because the room is not perfectly square
Because boxes are sold in tens

subtopics.title: How Many Days Does the Tank Give You

questions.question: Forgetting to halve the diameter before squaring makes the volume answer:
The tank holding 2,463 m³ holds, in litres:
Which statement correctly contrasts the two rounding decisions in this lesson?
options: Both round up, because you must always be safe
Materials round UP because you must have enough; days and whole items round DOWN because you cannot have part of one
Both round down, because shops do not sell fractions
Rounding depends only on whether the decimal is above or below 0,5

questions.question: What should the final line of a measurement answer look like?
options: Just the number, since the working shows the rest
A sentence a real family could act on — how many days, tins or rands
